chunks: From him, from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام, who said:
It is not upon the bondwomen to cover themselves with a head-cover in the salat, and it is not proper for a woman to perform salat except in two garments.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual prayer in which the ruling applies
key_terms.الْإِمَاءِ: bondwomen; female slaves referred to in the ruling
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ: the woman to whom the dress ruling in prayer refers
key_terms.ثَوْبَيْنِ: two garments required here as proper attire
key_terms.يَتَقَنَّعْنَ: to cover themselves with a head-cover or veil

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a woman's clothing in salat and whether bondwomen must wear a head-cover?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal distinction regarding women's dress in salat, indicating that bondwomen are not required to cover with a head-cover in prayer. It also states that a woman should not perform salat except in two garments, expressing a ruling on proper attire for prayer.
